llm.summary: This Kia Access skill is transparent and purpose-aligned, but it handles sensitive car account credentials and vehicle commands, so users should protect its configuration carefully.

dimensions.detail: Kia credentials, vehicle location access, and write modes are sensitive but proportionate to the requested vehicle-control functionality and are disclosed in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup runs the external npm package via npx and places Kia credentials in MCP environment config; this is coherent for an MCP integration, but users should trust the package source and avoid project configs that may be committed or shared.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger language is broad within Kia vehicle requests, but it remains scoped to Kia account vehicle reads or commands and the artifact repeatedly requires confirmation for writes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact discloses a long-lived local remember-me token, a plaintext refresh-token export tool, and a confirmation-gated local forget-session tool; this is sensitive persistence but not hidden.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's ability to read Kia vehicle status, location, charge state, and send confirmation-gated climate, charging, lock, and unlock commands matches its stated Kia Access MCP purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the kiaaccess-mcp package and are comfortable giving it access to your Kia account. Prefer user-scoped private configuration, do not commit .mcp.json with credentials or tokens, start with KIA_WRITE_MODE=none if you only need reads, and use door-unlock or token-export features only after explicit approval.
llm.findings:
[AS2] expected: The artifact does instruct users to provide Kia credentials through MCP config, which is expected for this integration but should be handled carefully because it can enable account and vehicle access.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger phrase covers any Kia vehicle read or command request, but it is still tied to the skill's stated purpose and commands are described as confirmation-gated.
